findings.title: Rejected GREEN's 3x historical-issuance scan cap is still live and applies only to creator-trusted-v1, inverting the accepted design
findings.evidence: packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:4492 sets `const maxHistoricalIssuanceRows = context.maxEpochVertices * 3` with no profile predicate; the enclosing countHistoricalIssuanceRow (:4487-4494) and HistoricalIssuanceContext (:4473-4479) carry no profile field, and the sole construction site openHistoricalIssuance (:8450-8478) is ungated. Introduced by rejected GREEN 1063feca (git show 1063feca -- packages/node/src/v3-live.ts, replacing `return context.count <= context.maxEpochVertices`) and not reverted by corrective GREEN 292fc14f. packages/node/src/internal/creator-transition-advance.ts:573-586 returns undefined unless exactly one legacy creator-retirement record is in the closure, and .logs/d110c-0c1f5b0r-design-3a156aca/design.md:180 states settlement-profile closures emit neither the v1 aggregate nor the legacy retirement record; therefore the context, and the raised cap, exist only under creator-trusted-v1. Accepted design.md:335-337 asks for `(rollback + 1) x maxEpochVertices` under the settlement profile and design.md:547-548 freezes creator-trusted-v1 byte-for-byte; .logs/d110c-0c1f5b0d-review-307825ef/review-ledger.md:36-39 already ruled 'Raising the legacy cap is not accepted as byte-for-byte compatibility'. The cap is a hard admission bound: exceeding it returns admission-rejected at v3-live.ts:5733-5741, record-rejected at :6956-6962, and truncates pages at :5167 and :7101. .logs/d110c-0c1f5b0d-corrective-green-292fc14f/deferred.md:8-9 and plan lines 18452 and 99352-99353 describe the legacy one-epoch bound as unchanged/preserved, which is false of the tree, so no slice owns the revert.
findings.required_action: Revert v3-live.ts:4492 to `return context.count <= context.maxEpochVertices` (or gate the raised bound behind settlementProfileFor(...) === "v1" and derive it from the frozen active-plus-two-rollback law rather than a literal 3), under a corrective tests-only RED that fails on the legacy profile. If the revert is deferred, deferred.md and the plan reslice must be corrected to state that creator-trusted-v1 currently runs a raised cap and to name the owning slice for the revert, instead of asserting the one-epoch bound is preserved.

findings.title: Retained 136/124 gates keep the invalidated source-text reachability oracle green and pin the raised cap
findings.evidence: tests/phase-6b-d110c-0c1f5b0d-reclamation-red.test.ts is listed in both retained selectors (.logs/d110c-0c1f5b0d-corrective-green-292fc14f/retained-files.md:7 and :23) and is counted inside the 136/136 and 124/124 GREEN claims. Its :300-304 case, titled 'invokes authenticated pruning only from the production cleanup path that owns verified adoption gates', asserts only `toContain(".pruneAuthenticatedSettledPrefix(")` and `toContain("planClosedEpochCleanup(")`; grep confirms the sole v3-live.ts occurrence of planClosedEpochCleanup( is the comment at :3192, which is precisely what review-ledger.md:17-20 invalidated. That directly contradicts .logs/d110c-0c1f5b0d-corrective-green-292fc14f/README.md:21-24 ('no comment, source-text match, or manufactured receipt is used as reachability evidence here'). The same file's :306-313 asserts the countHistoricalIssuanceRow body must NOT contain 'context.count <= context.maxEpochVertices' and :315-320 requires it to match `maxEpochVertices\s*\*\s*3|maxHistoricalIssuanceRows|...`, so the retained-green matrix mechanically defends the P1 above and forbids the plain restoration the accepted review demanded.
findings.required_action: Either correct or explicitly exclude the three invalidated cases (:300-304, :306-313, :315-320) from the retained selectors and re-record retained-core.json / retained-settlement-recovery.json with the new counts, or replace them with behavioral assertions. Whichever is chosen, the GREEN packet must disclose that the retained totals previously included a source-substring reachability oracle satisfied by a comment.

findings.title: Maintenance capability is a published package subpath and a Symbol.for global registry but is still documented as package-internal
findings.evidence: packages/issuance-store/package.json:26-29 exports './maintenance', while packages/issuance-store/src/maintenance.ts:81 and :95 both state 'This is a package-internal owner hook'. The registry at maintenance.ts:46-77 is installed on globalThis under Symbol.for('@ts-drp/issuance-store/pruning-maintenance-v1') and exposes resolve()/bind() to any same-realm code. review-ledger.md:31-35 explicitly required this be stated as an intentional capability surface rather than called package-private; the corrective GREEN did not touch maintenance.ts and no evidence file (source-shape.md, deferred.md, README.md) records the disposition. The exact-store identity test at tests/phase-6b-d110c-0c1f5b0d-corrective-red.test.ts:116-128 correctly denies copies and proxies, so the binding is sufficient under the trusted same-realm model, but the doc comment misdescribes the surface.
findings.required_action: Correct the two JSDoc comments to describe the published ./maintenance subpath as an intentional same-realm capability surface, and record that disposition in the evidence packet.

findings.title: Nothing in the store binds an authenticated deletion to a checkpoint; commitQcRef and snapshotManifestDigest are shape-validated but never used
findings.evidence: packages/issuance-store/src/maintenance.ts:189-195 validates commitQcRef.byteLength/digest and snapshotManifestDigest, and :309-310/:316 copy them into the receipt, but neither value appears in any predicate in conformance.ts:366-451, browser-issuance-store.ts:702-849 or node-issuance-store.ts:779-928. The store also has no terminalThrough input, so a caller passing a throughAuthorSequence above the author's settled boundary would delete displaced source rows that design.md:324-326 says are 'never silently terminal'; only settlementPlanPermitsAuthenticatedPruning (maintenance.ts:110-127) partially covers this, and it permits unlinked 'expire' entries by design.
findings.required_action: Record in the f5b integration contract that throughAuthorSequence must equal the authenticated terminalThrough and that the store performs no checkpoint authentication despite the method name; f5b's RED must cover a caller passing a boundary above terminalThrough.

findings.title: Idempotent replay returns before the epoch ceiling and echoes an unvalidated closedEpoch into the receipt
findings.evidence: In all three backends the watermark-equals-through early return (conformance.ts:384-389, browser-issuance-store.ts:738-744, node-issuance-store.ts:809-816) runs before `from` is computed and before the per-row epoch check, and createDurableIssuancePruningReceipt (maintenance.ts:309) copies input.closedEpoch verbatim. A replay with a wrong closedEpoch therefore yields a success receipt asserting a ceiling that was never applied. The retained consumer at v3-live.ts:3196-3208 compares deletedAuthorSequenceRange, prunedThroughAuthorSequence and observedLineage but not closedEpoch.
findings.required_action: Document that a pruning receipt is not evidence of the epoch ceiling that governed the deletion, and have f5b compare closedEpoch (or re-derive it from the checkpoint) wherever a receipt is consumed as proof.

findings.title: Authenticated prefix length is unbounded inside a single strict transaction
findings.evidence: The prefix is bounded only by durableIssuanceLineageConsumed: browser-issuance-store.ts:780-814 issues two IDB gets per ordinal and one delete per ordinal for the whole from..through range inside one strict readwrite transaction; node-issuance-store.ts:846-899 pages the SELECTs by 64 but holds one BEGIN IMMEDIATE for the entire range; conformance.ts:414-448 loops the full range. design.md:330-331 accepts 'any number of old epochs', so a first prune after long uptime is one very large transaction with no maximum batch.
findings.required_action: Have f5b bound the per-invocation prefix (or prune per epoch) when it wires the production caller, and record the chosen bound; no backend change is required if the caller guarantees it.

findings.title: Retained reclaimV3RuntimeKernel block still hardcodes the rejected legacy-first shape and carries a false authority comment
findings.evidence: packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:3181-3211 (from rejected GREEN 1063feca) calls pruneAuthenticatedSettledPrefix under settlementProfileFor(...) === 'v1' using a caller-supplied legacy receipt, so the watermark already equals throughAuthorSequence and the call is a guaranteed no-op replay. Its comment at :3192 asserts 'The receipt pair reaches this owner only after planClosedEpochCleanup(...) has authenticated adoption, rollback retention, availability and expected-head state', which review-ledger.md:17-20 found untrue since planClosedEpochCleanup has no product caller. Plan lines 99345-99351 require f5b's RED to prove authenticated pruning is the first deleting mutation and no legacy prune runs first, which this retained block structurally contradicts.
findings.required_action: f5b must delete or restructure this block and its comment when it wires the genuine every-peer invocation; until then the false authority comment should not remain as the only documentation of the gating contract.
